newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major attacks "fancy face" of Labour.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major attacks "fancy face" of Labour.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major accused the opposition Labour Party of conducting their May 1 election campaign on a "false prospectus".
"They are presenting, in my judgement, a completely false face to the public," Major said in an interview with Sunday's News of the World.
"The fancy face of Labour is not the reality of Labour and could not be the reality of Labour in government," he said.

Major said that Tony Blair's New Labour would not have carried out Conservative policies on tax-cutting, deregulation and the privatisation of major state industries "and they would not do it if they ever came to power."
He said taxes, spending, interest and mortgage rates would rise if Labour took power in the May 1 election.
"If people think it's safe to vote Labour then I believe they'd be in for a very nasty shock," he said.
Major said he was "utterly convinced" that the Conservatives could win the election.
"We've got the best economy that anyone has ever seen in this country for 70 years...The underlying message, quite simple, is that Britain's booming. Don't let Labour blow it."

Major said that he would reject a European single currency if it was "not right" when it came to a decision, but that Britain must stay at the talks table with other members of the European Union to "stop other people doing foolish things".
